meta.title: Where to stay in Singapore: shophouse hotels and quiet neighbourhoods | Five Foot Way
meta.description: The neighbourhoods we choose for our guests, from shophouse hotels in Chinatown to quieter streets near the Botanic Gardens and the east coast.

hero.title: Where to stay
hero.sub: Choose the neighbourhood first, then the hotel. Where you sleep decides how early you can walk.

intro.text: We place guests in small hotels in the old neighbourhoods, close to an MRT station and a hawker centre, so that an early walk starts at the door and a midday rest is ten minutes away. The hotels below are placeholders while we finalise our partner list: the neighbourhoods and the reasoning are real.

note: **These are placeholder names.** We have not yet published our partner hotels. Each card describes the kind of stay we book in that neighbourhood. Ask us for current recommendations through the [enquiry form](@enquire).
listText: Each of these is matched to a neighbourhood and a kind of trip. We will suggest specific hotels, with current rates, once we know your dates.

items.name: Shophouse Hotel A
text: A restored row of shophouses with small rooms, high ceilings and a five-foot way at the door. Three hawker centres within ten minutes and three MRT lines nearby. For first visits and short stays.

items.name: Terrace Hotel B
text: Peranakan terrace houses on a quiet hill a few minutes from Orchard Road. Convenient for the Botanic Gardens at dawn.

items.name: Boutique Hotel C
text: A small hotel in a converted shophouse among the Peranakan streets, twenty minutes from Changi. For layovers, late flights and anyone who likes to eat.

items.name: Garden Hotel D
text: Low-rise rooms among old trees near the Botanic Gardens, quiet at night. For walkers and families who want space and a pool.

items.name: Riverside Hotel E
text: A converted riverside warehouse on the quiet upper river, close to the river walk and the Civic District. For longer city stays.
